inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,763 logical lines of the normalized article. The source develops a scale-dependent phase diagram for typical short-interval moments and maxima of the Riemann zeta function, distinguishes mesoscopic and macroscopic correlation geometry, and proves matching bounds through moment estimates, discretization, removal of common small-prime modes, off-axis transfer, mollification, and a multiscale second-moment argument. The prose and proof architecture are recoverable from the text layer; several displayed formulas are fragmented by PDF extraction, so exact symbolic reuse of those spans should be checked against the retained scan.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the short-interval moment and maximum results, their phase transition, interval-regime distinction, and conditional range.

sections_inspected.label: 1.1 Maxima and moments over large intervals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets the global maximum and moment benchmarks against which the local problem is posed.

sections_inspected.label: 1.2 Maxima and moments over short intervals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces freezing, defines the exponent and maximum phase diagram, states the main theorems, and develops REM and interval-scale heuristics.

sections_inspected.label: 1.3 Relations to other models
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates the zeta problem to CUE characteristic polynomials, Gaussian multiplicative chaos, and randomized Dirichlet polynomials.

sections_inspected.label: Notation and 1.4 Outline of the proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Fixes conventions and explains the upper/lower proof pipelines, logarithmic covariance, branching scales, and the three interval geometries.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1 Moment estimates
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds unconditional and conditional moment inputs, truncated exponentials, Euler-product estimates, exceptional-set control, and a mollified-zeta moment bound.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2 Discretization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers continuous suprema to logarithmic grids, constructs a smoothed zeta approximation, and controls small-prime and mollified processes.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3.1 Upper bounds for theta at least zero
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives maximum and moment upper bounds by moment optimization and high-point level decomposition.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3.2 Upper bounds for negative theta
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Removes the common small-prime component and repeats the optimized high-point argument with the reduced effective variance.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Lower bounds and 3.1 Reduction off-axis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the lower targets, proves a strip convexity tool, constructs an analytic rectangle localizer, and transfers off-axis moments back to the critical line.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2 Mollification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs a theta-sensitive mollifier and proves it uniformly approximates the inverse of zeta on the whole interval.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3 Approximation of the mollifier
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces the finite mollifier by an exponential prime-power polynomial with a negligible high-factor tail.

sections_inspected.label: 3.4 Proofs of the lower bounds
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Decomposes primes into scales, turns high-point entropy into free energy, executes one- and two-point second-moment estimates, and assembles moment and maximum lower bounds.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A: Useful estimates
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies prime-sum, Dirichlet mean-value, Gaussian-moment, covariance, tail, and crude high-moment estimates used throughout.

accepted_units.title: Typical short-interval moments and maxima have an interval-dependent freezing transition
accepted_units.why_material: The abstract compresses the paper's main semantic claim: an explicit exponent changes from quadratic to linear at a critical beta, with different mesoscopic and macroscopic forms caused by correlation geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Read as a result summary; exact definitions of the exponents and conditional ranges are supplied later in lines 174-229.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is clear, but the displayed integrals and exponents are split across lines; verify exact notation against the retained PDF before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Global maxima are poorly controlled while global moment growth has a stable conjectural law
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the unresolved pointwise/global-maximum scale with the random-matrix moment conjecture and its arithmetic factor, motivating moments as a better-calibrated observable.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Lindelof/RH/unconditional comparison and the established ranges supporting the global moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Historical prose is recoverable; displayed bounds and powers are extraction-sensitive and require scan verification for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Freezing on fixed intervals prompts a scale-of-interval phase diagram
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from a fixed local interval to lengths log^theta T and asks exactly how long freezing persists, separating a structural scale question from a single special case.
accepted_units.context_note: The fixed-interval conjectures and prior leading-order results are setup for the paper's all-theta theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose makes the transition clear; the piecewise moment display at lines 162-166 should be scan-checked if quoted symbolically.

accepted_units.title: Piecewise moment exponent encodes quadratic bulk and linear frozen regimes
accepted_units.why_material: Defines m(theta), f_theta(beta), and beta_c(theta), then states matching probabilistic moment bounds and explains domination by rare near-maximum values above criticality.
accepted_units.context_note: The upper bound is unconditional only through theta at most three, unless RH is assumed; this limitation belongs to the moment input rather than the lower-bound mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Material depends on the piecewise display and inequalities; prose recovers their roles, but exact radicals, powers, and inequality directions require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Local maximum exponent changes from linear to square-root interval growth
accepted_units.why_material: States the maximum analogue of the moment phase diagram, with the same conditional boundary for long intervals.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is later deduced in each direction from optimized moment or high-point estimates.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed probability statements are legible in structure but formula extraction swaps some fractions; check the scan for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: REM predicts leading exponents but correlations control subleading behavior
accepted_units.why_material: Combines Selberg Gaussianity, the inverse-log discretization scale, and the number of grid points to derive a REM baseline, then identifies log correlations as the obstruction to treating all samples as independent.
accepted_units.context_note: For positive theta the paper proposes many independent branching walks, explaining why REM survives at leading and conjecturally subleading order but not at fluctuation level.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core reasoning is prose-supported; exact centering constants in Conjecture 1.3 are display-dependent and should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Negative theta separates a shared Gaussian mode from a later branching process
accepted_units.why_material: Models a mesoscopic interval as one random walk up to the common scale followed by branching, predicting both the leading maximum and an additional shared Gaussian fluctuation.
accepted_units.context_note: This heuristic is later realized analytically by cutting off primes below the theta-dependent scale.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The shared-mode interpretation is clear in prose; the exact fluctuation display is extraction-fragmented and needs PDF confirmation.

accepted_units.title: CUE, multiplicative chaos, and randomized prime sums realize complementary parts of the zeta picture
accepted_units.why_material: Shows which probabilistic representations capture moments, extrema, multiplicative chaos, freezing, and Gibbs geometry, while noting that CUE has no obvious macroscopic-interval analogue.
accepted_units.context_note: These are analogies and prior-model results, not proofs of the zeta theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primarily prose; exact normalized chaos measures and parameter ranges depend on displayed formulas and should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Upper bounds combine pointwise moments with logarithmic-grid discretization and scale removal
accepted_units.why_material: Explains the common upper-bound skeleton and why negative theta requires replacing zeta by zeta times the exponential of the removed small-prime polynomial.
accepted_units.context_note: The extra theta contribution in the negative-theta exponent is traced to the effective variance after removing common scales.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose supports the strategy; formulas (1.18)-(1.22) are line-broken and exact powers should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: Lower bounds factor through off-axis transfer, mollification, and a log-correlated prime field
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies a reusable three-step route: dominate an off-axis moment by a critical-line integral, approximate the off-axis zeta by an exponential prime sum, then analyze its covariance.
accepted_units.context_note: The explicit entire-function localizer handles very short intervals where a naive Poisson-kernel argument is technically inefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The chain of reductions is prose-clear; exact integration windows, sigma shift, and covariance sum are formula-dependent and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Prime blocks form random-walk increments whose branching time is set by point separation
accepted_units.why_material: Turns logarithmic covariance into an approximate tree: equal-variance prime blocks remain shared until log of inverse separation, producing one truncated tree for negative theta, one tree at theta zero, and a forest for positive theta.
accepted_units.context_note: The three geometries explain the distinct exponent formulas and motivate the later scale-block second-moment proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and figure caption recover the mechanism; the diagram layout is extraction-dependent and should be consulted in the PDF for visualization.

accepted_units.title: Conditional deterministic control and unconditional average control require different moment inputs
accepted_units.why_material: Separates RH-based deterministic prime-sum domination from the unconditional strategy of discarding large-prime contributions on average, and introduces finite exponential truncation as the bridge to Dirichlet polynomials.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite truncation is parameterized by the number of prime factors and a multiplicative coefficient function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The methodological contrast is clear; the deterministic bound and multinomial identity are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: A truncated exponential becomes a short multiplicative Dirichlet polynomial with Euler-product moments
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the algebraic encoding used to turn exponential prime factors into finite polynomials whose mean square factors and exposes the effective variance through the prime number theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the clean base case for the more intricate zeta-times-polynomial moment estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on extracted coefficient displays; scan verification is recommended for exact subscripts and restrictions.

accepted_units.title: Mixed zeta-polynomial moments reduce to a gcd-lcm Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a mean-square formula for zeta times a Dirichlet polynomial, removes excessive-factor tails by Chernoff/Rankin weighting, and evaluates the remaining gcd-lcm structure through an Euler product and contour representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The reusable mechanism is the conversion of a coupled arithmetic moment into local prime factors, not the routine term-by-term algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several long displays are fragmented; the prose validates the reduction and bounds, but exact local factors and exponents require PDF inspection.

accepted_units.title: High moments make exponential truncation uniform on a good event and yield the mollified moment bound
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the exceptional large-prime-polynomial event, applies Young's inequality to split the mollified zeta power, and combines two polynomial estimates to prove the key negative-theta moment bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The event bounds the removed prime polynomial; its complement is suppressed using high moments and the fourth zeta moment.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof logic is prose-recoverable; exact Young exponents, truncation coefficients, and log powers are display-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation samples a Dirichlet polynomial on an inverse-log grid
accepted_units.why_material: Proves a deterministic inequality transferring a continuous short-interval supremum to weighted grid values, using a compactly supported cutoff, Fourier decay, Holder's inequality, and Poisson summation.
accepted_units.context_note: The grid size grows like the interval length times log T; the tail is made negligible by choosing a sufficiently large decay exponent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument is clear in prose, but the exact sampling denominator and Fourier-transform normalization require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A contour-defined smoothing turns zeta into a discretizable finite Dirichlet polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs an explicit compact smoothing by Mellin inversion, shifts the contour to isolate zeta, bounds the displaced line, and combines the result with grid discretization.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the bridge from the abstract polynomial discretization to zeta itself uniformly in the relevant strip.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The smoothing definition and contour formulas are extraction-sensitive; verify the exact kernel, contour, and error exponent against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Second moments plus discretization give a theta-uniform preliminary maximum bound
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how even a suboptimal tail bound can control parameter-dependent interval lengths by first handling impossible extreme lengths and then applying a grid union bound with the zeta second moment.
accepted_units.context_note: This bound is later used to control remote tails in the off-axis unsmoothing argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical use is clear; exact thresholds and powers in Corollary 2.10 need scan checking.

accepted_units.title: Small primes are nearly rigid across a negative-theta interval
accepted_units.why_material: Refines the generic prime-polynomial maximum bound by decomposing a short-interval process into its value at one point and a small increment, then proving exponential tails for both via moments and discretization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Interval length determines correlation geometry and therefore the phase diagram
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The piecewise exponents can be read as consequences of three geometries: a shortened tree after a shared prefix for negative theta, one log-correlated tree at theta zero, and a forest of nearly independent trees for positive theta.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a leading-order, source-internal synthesis; the source explicitly warns that correlations still affect proofs and fluctuations, and it does not establish the conjectured subleading laws.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Removing common small primes is both a probabilistic coarse-graining and an analytic mollification step
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For negative theta, the same low-prime contribution is nearly constant across the interval, so deleting it reveals the effective branching field and reduces the variance entering moment optimization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The equivalence is approximate and high-probability; it depends on the interval and prime scales chosen in the paper.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The upper and lower phase transitions share an entropy-energy variational mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Upper high-point stratification and lower high-point volume estimates optimize the same height reward plus entropy cost, with an interior optimizer below criticality and the maximal-height endpoint above it.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The two directions use different analytic inputs, and matching leading exponents do not supply the finer freezing distribution or Gibbs-measure law.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The lower-bound proof is a sequence of controlled representation changes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A critical-line moment is compared with an off-axis localized norm, zeta is inverted by a finite mollifier, the mollifier is converted to an exponential prime field, and that field is decomposed into near-Gaussian scale blocks before second-moment analysis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Every arrow is probabilistic and parameter-dependent; this synthesis does not license exchanging the order of reductions or omitting their good events and error budgets.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Discretization is the common bridge from averaged control to interval-uniform control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Inverse-log grid sampling repeatedly converts Dirichlet-polynomial moment or L2 information into control of maxima across intervals whose number of effective sites grows with theta.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The bridge requires a finite polynomial approximation, beta at least one in its direct form, and tail/error estimates strong enough to pay for the grid size.
